Title: Pro-Trump  deniers crash against 'blue tsunami'
Article:
CONSPIRACY THEORISTS
FOR  months, conspiracy-peddling supporters of President Donald Trump spread baseless theories that the vote would be rigged. But those claims all but dried up after Democrats swept the US midterm elections.
Political pundits had anticipated a wave of legal challenges from election deniers seeking to contest the results of Tuesday's vote, or efforts by Trump himself to tilt the outcome in his favour — as he did when he tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat.
But none of that materialised.
And evidence-free claims of fraud slowed to a trickle after what observers called the decisive "blue tsunami" of Democratic victories that handed the party control of both chambers of Congress.
Trump's acceptance of the results, signalling he would not challenge his Republican Party's sweeping defeat, set the tone for many of his loyalists to follow suit.
"Election day 2026 featured a few rumours about election integrity.
"However, election denialism was not a core narrative used to explain the sweeping victories by Democrats once they became apparent," said the University of Washington's Center for an Informed Public.
"Absent a political elite to champion election denialism, rumouring about election integrity has not coalesced into a coherent or significant narrative to explain election results."
Many analysts said the scale of the Democratic victory — widely seen as a repudiation of Trump's political agenda — may have played a role.
However, David Becker, executive director of the nonpartisan Center for Election Innovation and Research, argued that fraud claims persisted in the past even when the president's preferred candidates lost by large margins.
"I don't know necessarily that margin of victory makes much difference to those who have profited off  the economy of grift around election conspiracies for quite some time," Becker said.
"It might be that politics overall in the nation have changed to some degree, and that creates a different incentive structure."
It also did not help that many election deniers on the ballot lost their races — and chose not to challenge the results.
Among them was Andy Biggs, one of the Republican politicians who joined Trump in challenging the 2020 election results after his defeat to Joe Biden.
After losing Arizona's gubernatorial race, Biggs conceded to incumbent Democrat Katie Hobbs, making no mention of voter fraud and instead blaming what he perceived as a low voter turnout.
"We just didn't get our turnout quite as full as we wanted to," he said in comments reported by US media.
Even conservative influencers — including prominent supporters of Trump's Make America Great Again  movement who have been vocal election sceptics — appeared subdued.
Ahead of the midterm elections, some sceptics went so far as to call for a "national emergency", urging Trump to grant himself "king-like powers" over the midterms, according to the left-leaning watchdog Media Matters for America.
"I have been banging the drum of rigged and stolen elections since 2020, but that is not why we lost the midterms," conservative political commentator Rogan O'Handley wrote to his 2.3 million followers on X.
"We lost because we failed to fix the things voters sent us to do... Lower gas and food prices and stop the Iran war."
Media Matters' John Knefel cautioned against "premature" hopes that "the election denial fever has permanently broken".
"Rejecting Democratic Party wins remains a core, foundational element of the movement that Trump built and will likely continue to be one for the foreseeable future," he said.
But striking a note of optimism, Becker said "American voters are tired" of evidence-free election denialism.
"A smaller number of election sceptics ran this time than in past cycles, and there seem to be substantially less stomach for these claims among voters," said Pamela Smith, president of the nonpartisan nonprofit Verified Voting.
Citing an independent poll, Smith added: "Most voters are interested in other issues — fraud in elections does not seem to be a driver for deciding their vote."
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Zahid: Malaysia-Türkiye US$10 billion trade target "achievable"
Article:
ISTANBUL: Malaysia and Turkiye's trade target of US$10 billion by 2030 is achievable, especially through the procurement of defence and security equipment.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the balance of trade between both countries is currently in Malaysia's favour.
"From the effort of both countries, the target is achievable, especially from Malaysia, in procuring defence and security equipment," he said.
Zahid was speaking at a panel session titled "Turkiye: From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor" at the 2026 TRT World Forum here today.
Other panellists included Foundation for Political, Economic and Social Research (SETA) Foreign Policy Studies director Prof Murat Yesiltas; Atlantic Council non-resident senior fellow Dr Rich Outzen; American Arab Center president Farah Al-Atassi; and United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations Jean-Pierre Lacroix.
The forum, themed "A World Without a Center: Who Leads When the Rules Run Out?", brings together political leaders, policymakers, academics, media practitioners and civil society representatives to discuss global issues.
The forum was launched by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
He said Malaysia has taken delivery of Littoral Mission Ships and unmanned aerial vehicles from Turkiye. This, he said, would strengthen ties not only in defence and security, but also in trade.
"I think extra effort will be taken by both countries to achieve the target," he said.
Meanwhile, Zahid said Malaysia views defence cooperation with Turkiye as a strategic choice and not just a procurement exercise, as it involves the transfer of knowledge and technology.
"Turkiye occupies a strategic position connecting Europe, West Asia, Central Asia and surrounding regions. That is why I think close collaboration between Malaysia and Turkiye is important," he said.
Zahid said Malaysia also viewed Turkiye's status as a 12th Asean Dialogue Partner as an opportunity for more structured cooperation that delivers tangible benefits, rather than adding another diplomatic platform.
He said military diplomacy was also important to keep Southeast Asia peaceful and politically stable, and to prevent major powers from influencing Asean member states.
Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, is in Turkiye for a four-day working visit from Nov 5 to 8.
Malaysia and Turkiye established diplomatic relations on June 17, 1964, and have since maintained close ties in politics, the economy, trade and education.
Malaysia is one of Turkiye's largest trading partners in Southeast Asia.
Bilateral trade stands at US$5.6 billion, and both countries aim to raise it to US$10 billion by 2030 following an agreement between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Erdogan in January.

Title: The high price of corruption in private sector
Article:
IN January last year, two former Sea Tackle Sdn Bhd directors, namely Teo Tzi Sin and Wong Poh Wah, were each fined RM100,000 for the offence of abusing their positions by using RM200,000 in company funds to pay themselves unauthorised bonuses.
They were charged under Section 218(1)(c) of the Companies Act 2016, read with Section 34 of the Penal Code.
The case clearly sends a clear message that company directors must carry out their functions and use their given authority in the company's interests, and not for personal benefit.
Under Section 218 of Companies Act 2016, directors and company officers who misuse their positions to benefit themselves or others, or to harm the company, may face up to five years in prison, a fine of up to RM3 million, or both.
But abuse of power does not happen only when directors take company money.
It can also involve  directors awarding contracts to  friends, family members or business associates, hiding personal interests, manipulating financial records, submitting false invoices and using confidential company information for personal gain.
The problem does not lie only with large corporations.
According to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission, corruption involving private-sector entities in 2025 amounted to approximately RM520 million, comprising RM124 million from listed companies, RM383 million from non-listed companies and RM11 million from sole proprietorships.
Under Section 213 of the Companies Act 2016, directors must act honestly, make decisions for proper reasons and put the company's interests first.
They must also use reasonable care, skill and attention when carrying out their duties. A director who breaks these legal duties may face up to five years in prison, a fine of up to RM3 million, or both.
Section 218 deals more directly with the misuse of a director's or company officer's position, company property, information or business opportunities for personal benefit or to harm the company.
The MACC Act 2009 also applies when corrupt payments are involved. Sections 16 and 17 deal with offering, giving, soliciting or receiving bribes by any person or by an agent.
Section 17A allows a company to be held liable when an associated person commits bribery to benefit the company. Section 23, meanwhile, deals with public officers who misuse their positions to obtain gratification.
It may also apply to officers of certain GLCs that qualify as public bodies under the act.
The Penal Code covers other offences, including criminal breach of trust, cheating, forgery, using false documents and falsifying company accounts.
The Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 covers market manipulation, false statements and insider trading, punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment and a minimum RM1 million fine.
One incident may involve several offences, but authorities must prove each offence; suspicious transactions alone does not mean someone is guilty. There is an important difference between making a poor business decision and deliberately breaking the law or committing error and fraud.
A director may make a business decision that turns out badly, which does not automatically mean that the director has committed a crime. However, directors must still take reasonable care and assess the risks before making decisions.
The situation is different when someone deliberately cheats the company, misappropriates  money for personal use, accepts bribes or hides dishonest transactions where such actions may amount to criminal offences.
Laws in the country do not provide for "carelessness and stupidity" to be charged as offences.
In Hong Kong, public officers can face up to seven years in prison and a fine for seriously abusing their positions or deliberately neglecting their duties without a valid excuse, in breach of public trust.
Malaysia should continue to examine whether its laws provide sufficient protection when serious failures of responsibility lead to the misuse or loss of public money. Any criminal charge, however, must be supported by evidence and a clearly established legal offence.
Laws alone cannot prevent corporate abuse. Companies need a strong leadership, a clear tone at the top, effective controls and people committed to acting with honesty and integrity.
The Attorney-General's Chambers carries out the prosecution of criminal cases.
Ultimately, company directors and senior executives are entrusted with money, assets and the confidence of shareholders, employees and the public.
They must never forget that their positions carry a huge responsibility, not personal privileges.
* The writer is president of Malaysian Integrity and Governance Society (MIG) and professor of criminology at HELP University

Title: Anwar open to foreign workers for oil palm harvesting, with mechanisation pledge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is open to approving foreign workers for oil palm harvesting, provided the plantation industry commits to reducing its reliance on migrant labour through mechanisation.
He also said any abuse of workers, including foreign workers, must be met with firm action.
Speaking at the 14th Malaysia Madani Scholars Forum today, Anwar was responding to a question from a plantation industry representative who said most planters had yet to receive their foreign worker quotas for this year.
Also on the panel were Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, SD Guthrie Bhd president and group chief executive officer Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad, and PNB Research Institute chief executive officer Dr Sarena Che Omar.
The representative said machines were already being used for fertilising and weeding, but none were yet available for harvesting oil palm fruit, a task that still relied on foreign labour.
He told Anwar that recruitment took about three months, with a further three months needed for training.
Production could be affected next year if workers were not secured now, particularly with El Niño and haze expected, he said.
Anwar said he would view the matter "sympathetically" and raise it with the minister concerned.
He said the government could approve foreign workers for harvesting, on condition that the industry committed to reducing its reliance on them through mechanisation.
He said major plantation companies had not invested sufficiently in mechanisation to reduce their workforce, even when profits were high.
"A company makes a billion in profit. Raise wages by RM20 a month, they attack it. Until we, the government, had to make it mandatory.
"That is why I say the economy must also be humane," he said.
Anwar said Malaysia could not allow oppression and the dehumanisation of workers in the pursuit of economic growth.
He cited foreign workers being housed in conditions resembling slavery a century ago.
"I cannot accept that," he said.
He said the government was negotiating with source countries individually to reduce recruitment costs, describing agents who held workers' passports as engaging in "modern slavery".
Anwar also said he had negotiated with Myanmar's president on the repatriation of its nationals in Malaysia.
"We have 200,000 Myanmar nationals here, including economic refugees. If they are sent back, human rights groups protest. If they stay here, the people protest," he said.
He said more than 10,000 had since been sent home under the arrangement.
"Anti-foreigner sentiment has sometimes become excessive and is no longer humane," he said.
"Tightening (the policy) will affect certain industries. Loosening it creates serious economic and social problems."
Last month, Anwar said 10,493 Myanmar nationals had been repatriated by air and sea following talks with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing during the latter's official visit to Malaysia.
Myanmar had also
agreed to take back
between 3,000 and 4,000 of its nationals held at immigration depots, at its own expense.
In November 2024, the government
approved a one-off special quota
of 24,570 foreign workers for 143 plantation companies to address labour shortages in the sector.
In February 2023, Anwar called for an
end to the use of agents
in foreign worker recruitment, saying the high costs involved amounted to modern slavery.

Title: Zahid, Erdogan discuss Malaysia-Türkiye ties, trade expansion
Article:
ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi paid a courtesy call on Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan today.
The meeting, which began at 4pm local time (9pm Malaysian time), lasted about 30 minutes and was held at the Istanbul Congress Centre after the 2026 TRT World Forum opening ceremony.
On bilateral ties, both sides looked forward to strengthening relations following the establishment of the High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council, whose inaugural meeting was held in Ankara in Jan this year.
The discussion also covered raising the bilateral trade target from US$5.6 billion in 2025 to US$10 billion by 2030.
Zahid also congratulated Turkiye on becoming Asean's 12th Dialogue Partner. Malaysia, he said, would work closely with Ankara as country coordinator.
On regional security, Zahid commended Turkiye's role as an interlocutor in Syria, Lebanon and Palestine, including Gaza.
He also praised Ankara's mediation in the Ukraine–Russia war through the "Istanbul Process" and voiced support for its backchannel diplomacy on the United States–Iran conflict, together with Pakistan, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.
Zahid also wished Turkiye success in hosting the  31st meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change summit in Antalya on Nov 11 and 12.
Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, is in Turkiye for a four-day working visit from Nov 5 to 8.

Title: Penang police probe viral video alleging patrol officers' misconduct
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Police have launched an investigation into a viral video alleging misconduct by patrol officers during an enforcement operation at Puncak Erskine in Tanjung Tokong.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police became aware of the footage circulating on social media today.
The video, showing mobile patrol vehicle (MPV) personnel on duty at Jalan Fettes, drew public attention after being shared by several Facebook accounts, including "Zippygiraffe43" and "M Riza Ni".
"A police report has been lodged by the personnel involved, denying any corrupt misconduct during the inspection," he said in a statement.
Rozak said police were investigating the allegations under Section 500 of the Penal Code for defamation and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
"At the same time, we will also investigate the personnel's compliance with standard operating procedures and internal disciplinary conduct," he said.
He advised the public against circulating the recording or speculating about the incident, saying this could interfere with investigations.
Anyone with information can contact the Northeast district police headquarters at 04-2181822 or investigating officer Inspector Zahirrudin Ismail at 014-3189026.

Title: Landslide closes Jalan Rawang-Kuala Selangor in Gombak
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Jalan Rawang-Kuala Selangor (B27) at Section 9.90 in Gombak has been closed to all vehicles following a landslide that damaged part of the road structure last night.
The incident was reported about 11pm, involving failures of both the upper and lower slopes, which caused part of the road structure to collapse.
The Selangor Public Works Department (PWD) said the landslide also brought down trees, blocking the entire road.
In a statement, it said the road closure was implemented by the Gombak District PWD, while information on alternative routes was shared through the Facebook pages of PWD Selangor and Gombak this morning.
"The incident is believed to have been caused by heavy rain, which led to a large amount of rainwater infiltrating the ground, increasing soil saturation and pore water pressure on the slopes.
"This caused slope instability and soil movement, resulting in the collapse and damage to part of the road structure," it said.
PWD Selangor said further investigations and technical assessments were under way to determine the actual cause of the incident.
It said a Traffic Management Plan (TMP) had also been activated, including the installation of signs indicating the full road closure and diversion routes to ensure road users' safety.
"Temporary tarpaulin sheets have also been installed on the affected roadside embankment and slope surfaces to prevent erosion and further landslides.
"Debris and fallen trees blocking the road following the upper slope failure are being cleared by the state road concessionaire.
"Continuous monitoring is being carried out by Gombak District PWD and the concessionaire to detect any active movement in the road structure and assess slope stability.
"Construction of a temporary diversion road in the affected area will be carried out to allow light vehicles to pass, subject to technical assessment and safety considerations, including the stability of the slopes," it said.
PWD Selangor said an announcement on the road's reopening would only be made after technical assessments confirmed that the landslide area was safe and the diversion road was suitable for light vehicles.
Road users have been advised to follow all traffic signs and diversion instructions for their safety.

Title: BSN customers may face difficulties withdrawing cash at other banks' ATMs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) customers may experience difficulties withdrawing cash from automated teller machines (ATMs) operated by other banks through the Malaysian Electronic Payment System (MEPS).
BSN said the disruption was due to high ATM transaction volumes.
It advised customers to use their BSN ATM cards at BSN machines temporarily.

Title: NST Leader: Avoiding the traps that turn Malaysians into drug mules
Article:
THAT 213 Malaysians were arrested overseas since 2024 for  alleged involvement as drug mules should be a sobering message for the country to take this matter far more seriously.
Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah has told the Dewan Rakyat that drug-trafficking syndicates are targeting young people, including students and graduates, with irresistible  financial and material incentives.
These syndicates must know  their targets are particularly susceptible to inducements for what may appear to be  harmless and routine tasks as human couriers.
Social media  also makes it all the more easier for drug traffickers to reach out to  potential victims, exploiting their gullibility and naivety.
Malaysians need to understand that ignorance  and being unaware of what they carry are unlikely to spare them from prosecution. As is  in Malaysia, many other countries have strict drug laws mandating lengthy prison sentences or even the death penalty upon conviction for trafficking.
A seemingly casual favour of carrying a package for someone  could cost those implicated  their freedom or even their lives.
Parents, universities and educational institutions must be particularly on the lookout and be proactive in educating young people about these syndicates' recruitment practices.
Awareness campaigns should go beyond the usual anti-drug messaging to include practical guidance on being cautious about suspicious job offers, verifying prospective employers and spotting red flags in online recruitment campaigns.
Educating the public on the issue should go hand in hand with enforcement action. The use of social media, e-commerce platforms and messaging applications by syndicates makes it necessary for the police, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, financial institutions and digital platforms to work in concert to identify and disrupt the nefarious recruitment networks.
This message must be drummed home: never accept luggage, parcels or other items from strangers or agree to transport goods overseas without first knowing precisely the contents.
The 213 cases should not be dismissed as isolated incidents or as merely the result of poor judgment.
The syndicates know only too well how trusting and obliging Malaysians can be, which are traits  they exploit to the fullest.
A  deliberate and increasingly sophisticated recruitment strategy is being employed by these international drug syndicates.
Malaysians must never allow the lure of quick and easy money, free holidays or other enticing perks to cloud their judgment.
The syndicates can be counted on to zero-in on  such momentary lapses in judgment in service of  their vile intentions.
The price of such mistakes is having to face long legal processes, which could lead to stiff prison sentences, or worse.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia hits 40th in global governance index, PM warns against complacency
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's rise to 40th place among 133 countries in the Chandler Good Government Index (CGGI) 2026 reflects the government's continued efforts to strengthen national administrative capacity, integrity and effectiveness, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
"This achievement is no excuse for us to be complacent. There is still room for improvement, particularly in strengthening inter-agency coordination and ensuring every policy and plan is implemented more efficiently and effectively," he said in a Facebook post today.
He said the government's priority remained building robust institutions, improving public service delivery and ensuring every development effort brought tangible benefits to the people.
"Ultimately, a government's success is not merely measured through its ranking in international indices, but through changes that can be felt in the people's lives," he added.
Malaysia climbed two places from 42nd in 2025 in the index, which evaluates national governance performance across seven core pillars.
The pillars are Leadership and Foresight, Attractive Marketplace, Financial Stewardship, Robust Laws and Policies, Global Influence and Reputation, Helping People Rise, and Strong Institutions.
In the 2026 ranking, Malaysia was behind China in 39th place, Slovakia in 38th and Saudi Arabia in 37th.
Singapore retained the top position for the fourth consecutive year since 2023, followed by Norway in second place and Denmark in third.

Title: Deepavali decorations bring Kota Baru family closer
Article:
KOTA BARU: With Deepavali just around the corner this Sunday, Murugaih M. Sathasivam has begun decorating his mother's home in Lundang, turning the family gathering place into a festive haven filled with warmth and togetherness.
The 51-year-old said decorating the house ahead of the Festival of Lights was a simple yet meaningful family tradition that brought his loved ones closer.
Assisted by his two sons, M. Sai Siddhart, 19, and Kavin, 13, as well as their cousin R. Hareetaran, 36, Murugaih said the preparations also provided an opportunity for family members to spend quality time together.
He said about 30 siblings and other relatives would usually gather at his mother's house to celebrate the festival.
"Every year, we decorate the house simply to welcome Deepavali. It is a family tradition that we have continued over the years.
"We usually have about 30 family members gathering here, so decorating the house is one of the ways we prepare for the celebration," he said.
The decorations, though modest, reflect the family's festive spirit and anticipation of the joyous occasion.
For Murugaih and his family, the preparations are not merely about beautifying the home but also about preserving a cherished tradition and strengthening family bonds.
"Every time Deepavali arrives, this house becomes a lively gathering spot where relatives come together to celebrate the festival.
"We will share meals and create lasting memories here," he said when met today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia has 6 months' rice supply, 8 months' fish stock amid cyberwar threat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has enough rice to last at least six months and fish for eight months should a cyberattack disrupt the country's communication networks, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
He said the government was prepared to distribute food supplies physically from farms if digital systems were disrupted.
Speaking at the 14th Malaysia Madani Scholars Forum today, Mohamad said the threat of cyber warfare was still at an early stage but was already real.
"The next war will be a cyber war. We must be mentally prepared for this," he said.
He likened the threat to the Star Wars films of the 1970s.
"We saw it as imagination, an illusion. But now it is really starting to happen," he said.
Mohamad asked the audience to imagine going a week without internet or television.
"We can sleep. But how would people order rice? Order fish? Order food supplies?" he said.
He said global power was no longer concentrated in the hands of a single party, with other players now capable of mounting cyber challenges against superpowers.
However, Mohamad assured the public that Malaysia was prepared for such disruptions.
"There is no need to panic, because we have enough rice stock for at least six months. We currently have enough fish for eight months and other food items are also available.
"But if there is a cyberattack and communications are cut, we are prepared through farms to send food supplies physically," he said.
Mohamad stressed that preparations were necessary even if such an attack never materialised.
"But preparation must be there and we must start educating the people to face cyber warfare in the future," he said.
He cited threats by an unnamed party to disrupt global supplies, including through cyber means, if its country came under attack again.
"If this happens, we will face the first Star War in the world," he said.
Mohamad claimed Europe had been harder hit by cyber warfare than countries in this region, citing incidents in which large quantities of vegetables were discarded after disruptions to electricity supplies caused food to spoil.
He also referred to protests involving about a million people in Paris, saying inflation and food security were among their concerns.
"Food and security have become a global agenda. We can have nuclear weapons, we can have modern weapons, but if there is no food, imagine what happens to a country," he said.
"So we must take cyber seriously and we hope it does not happen in Malaysia. That is our hope."
Also on the panel were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, SD Guthrie Bhd president and group chief executive officer Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad, and PNB Research Institute chief executive officer Dr Sarena Che Omar.
Last week, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi reaffirmed that Malaysia
had sufficient food supplies
to last 6 months.
Media reports have said several countries, including France, the United Kingdom and Japan, had advised households to maintain emergency supplies for at least 3 days amid concerns over conflicts, extreme weather and disruptions to critical services.

Title: [UPDATED] Najib remains in Kajang Prison as house arrest transfer stalls, lawyers confirm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak remains in Kajang Prison despite preparations for his transfer to house arrest, his lawyers confirmed tonight.
Messrs Shafee and Co said the transfer process was already under way when the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) issued a statement calling for the arrangement to be temporarily suspended.
"For the avoidance of doubt, our client has not yet left Kajang Prison.
"The process of releasing him into house arrest was under way when the A-GC Statement was issued," the firm said in a statement.
The lawyers maintained that all conditions imposed under Najib's conditional royal pardon had been fulfilled following the payment of his RM50 million fine earlier today.
They said the Kuala Lumpur High Court subsequently issued sealed orders to the officer in charge of Kajang Prison authorising Najib's immediate discharge in relation to the fine.
However, the A-GC called for the implementation of his house arrest to be deferred pending clarification of legal questions surrounding the conditional pardon and the court orders.
The A-GC said two possible interpretations had arisen over the effect of the RM50 million payment.
Under the first, payment would settle only the fine, with Najib continuing to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Under the second, payment could mean that the entire SRC International sentence, including the prison term, had been completed.
The chambers said the interpretation could also affect the commencement of Najib's separate prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case.
It maintained that the proposed deferment was not intended to challenge the King's decree but to ensure that the pardon and related court orders were implemented correctly.
Najib's lawyers rejected that explanation, insisting that the AGC had no basis to delay his transfer.
Najib was granted a conditional royal pardon by Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim on Sept 18, allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest, subject to payment of the fine and compliance with stipulated conditions.
He has been serving his sentence since Aug 23, 2022, following his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds.
His original 12-year prison sentence and RM210 million fine were reduced to six years and RM50 million respectively by the Pardons Board in 2024.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Najib's lawyers accuse A-GC of disregarding King's order, demand immediate house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyers have accused the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) of disregarding the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's order by delaying his transfer to house arrest.
Messrs Shafee and Co demanded that Najib be transferred immediately to his Taman Duta residence, maintaining that the conditions imposed under his conditional royal pardon had been fulfilled.
"We view the A-GC Statement as a disregard of His Majesty's order. Nothing in it provides any basis for keeping our client in Kajang Prison," the firm said in a statement.
"We therefore demand that our client be released immediately into house arrest at his residence, as His Majesty has ordered and the High Court has directed."
The lawyers argued that the A-GC had no legal authority to suspend a royal pardon or a sealed court order through a media statement.
"The Attorney General has no power of stay of His Majesty's royal prerogative of pardon," they said.
They maintained that any legal questions surrounding the High Court's orders should be referred to the court rather than used to delay Najib's transfer.
"If the A-GC has a real question over the Orders, its remedy is an application to the High Court, not a media statement," they said.
The legal team also accused the A-GC of raising questions over the conditional pardon only after Najib's RM50 million fine was paid, despite having seven weeks to seek clarification.
It claimed that the Attorney General had previously indicated that payment of the fine was the only outstanding requirement for Najib's house arrest.
The lawyers also noted that the Attorney General was a member of the Pardons Board and had attended its Sept 18 meeting, which advised the King on Najib's conditional pardon.
They argued that any concerns over the terms of the pardon should have been raised at that meeting.
The firm further alleged that the A-GC's position amounted to executive overreach and could constitute contempt or even treason against the King.
The lawyers demanded that the Attorney-General withdraw the A-GC statement immediately and called on the Commissioner General of Prisons to complete Najib's transfer without delay.
They also argued that keeping Najib at Kajang Prison on the basis of the A-GC statement would contravene Article 5(1) of the Federal Constitution.
Earlier today, Umno paid Najib's RM50 million fine at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, fulfilling a condition of the royal pardon granted by Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim on Sept 18.
The pardon allows Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to compliance with stipulated conditions.
However, the A-GC subsequently called for the implementation of house arrest to be temporarily deferred pending clarification of legal questions surrounding the pardon and the effect of the High Court's orders.
The A-GC said two possible interpretations had arisen over whether payment of the fine meant Najib's prison sentence remained in force or had been completed.
It said the distinction could affect the commencement of his separate prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case.
The A-GC maintained that the proposed deferment was not intended to challenge or set aside the King's decree, but to ensure that the pardon and related court orders were implemented correctly.

Title: [UPDATED] 'Illogical' to keep Najib in Kajang after home gazetted as prison, say lawyers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyers have questioned the Attorney-General's Chambers' (A-GC) move to delay his house arrest when his Taman Duta residence has already been gazetted as a prison.
Messrs Shafee and Co described the A-GC's position as illogical, arguing that transferring Najib to his residence would not remove him from lawful custody.
"It is therefore illogical for the A-GC, on the same day that the gazette declared our client's residence a prison, to insist that he remain in Penjara Kajang while it seeks clarification," the firm said in a statement.
The lawyers said the residence was now legally designated as a prison under the authority of the Commissioner General of Prisons.
"Moving our client there does not take him out of lawful custody. It moves him from one gazetted prison to another, as His Majesty has ordered," they said.
Earlier today, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail declared all buildings and areas at No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, Kuala Lumpur,
to be a prison
under Section 3 of the Prison Act 1995.
The declaration, published in the Federal Government Gazette as P.U. (B) 456/2026, covers an area measuring 4,558.975 square metres.
It designates the premises for the imprisonment or detention of persons lawfully in custody.
The lawyers argued that the gazette declaration removed any justification for keeping Najib at Kajang Prison while the A-GC sought clarification of his conditional royal pardon.
They said the A-GC's concerns over the legal effect of the pardon did not explain why Najib should remain in one gazetted prison rather than another.

The A-GC also said the interpretation could affect the commencement of Najib's separate prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case.
It maintained that the proposed deferment was intended to ensure the royal pardon and court orders were implemented correctly, rather than to challenge the King's decree.

Title: Najib's Taman Duta residence gazetted as prison
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's residence in Taman Duta here has been gazetted as a prison under the Prisons Act 1995.
The declaration, dated Nov 6, was made by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail under Section 3 of the Act.
According to the Federal Government Gazette, P.U. (B) 456/2026, the declaration covers all buildings and areas measuring 4,558.975 square metres at No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta.

The development follows Umno's payment of Najib's RM50 million fine earlier today, fulfilling a key condition of the royal pardon that allows him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Najib's lawyer, Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee, subsequently confirmed that the Kuala Lumpur High Court had issued an order allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his sentence at home.

In a statement, the A-GC said questions had arisen over whether payment of the RM50 million fine merely fulfilled the financial component of Najib's sentence or meant that his entire sentence in the SRC International case should be considered completed.

Najib, 73, has been serving his sentence since Aug 23, 2022, following his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds.

Title: Tech stocks suffer bloodbath as US midterms fuel AI fears
Article:
LONDON: Technology shares plunged Friday after an unnerving rout on Wall Street as fears grew that Democrats would accelerate a backlash against AI after their crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans in the US midterms.
The Tokyo and Seoul stock markets closed out their weeks with losses of six per cent following the Nasdaq's 5.5 per cent collapse on Thursday, its worst showing since April last year when Trump unveiled his wide-ranging global tariffs.
"The tech sell-off has intensified, with the pain of the brutal sell-off on Wall Street carried straight through to Asia and knocking sentiment in Europe," said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.
"Big worries are colliding -- the build-out of data centres looks set to slow, which risks shredding the spending spree underpinning the boom, right at the time that investors have become super nervous about returns on this massive investment," she said.
The London, Paris and Frankfurt stock markets shed around two per cent nearing the halfway stage despite featuring few technology firms.
Elsewhere, the dollar firmed before key US jobs data Friday, and oil prices steadied following steep declines this week.
Futures contracts pointed to a rebound on the Nasdaq later this afternoon, but further declines for the broad-based S&P 500.
Data centres have faced broad opposition from US voters across the political spectrum, and many midterm winners have pledged to put the brakes on such projects.
Analysts said investors were also spooked by a call from progressive US Senator Bernie Sanders for a national moratorium on their building.
The results compounded already heightened fears about the hundreds of billions firms had pumped into the sector and when they would see a return, while the recent spike in borrowing costs also fuelled concerns about their financial position.
Bloomberg said the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had collapsed around 16 per cent this week, putting it on course for its worst run since April last year.
On Seoul's Kospi stocks index, chip giant SK Hynix slumped 10 per cent and its rival Samsung lost 6.4 per cent.
The Kospi more than doubled in value between the end of December and mid-June, when it hit a record, but is down almost 50 per cent over the past four and a half months.
Tokyo dived six per cent Friday as Japanese tech investor SoftBank gave back more than 10 per cent, while chipmaker Kioxia collapsed 8.7 per cent and semiconductor tester Advantest retreated five per cent.
A 4.7 per cent drop for Taiwanese chip giant TSMC dragged down Taipei's Taiex.
"The blood is in the streets, folks," wrote Neil Wilson, analyst at Saxo Markets, though he added that the sell-off looked "overdone".
"The fear is a total momentum unwind as Democrats pace the frontier and kibosh data centre build-out," he said.

Title: Brent oil price benchmark set for biggest weekly drop since 2020
Article:
LONDON: Oil prices were set for a sharp weekly fall after the election losses of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party raised hopes of a de-escalation in the US-Israeli war on Iran and a stock market sell-off, though attacks on vessels in the Middle East continue to provide a floor to crude.
In a whiplash see-saw session on Friday, Brent crude futures for January were up 31 cents, or 0.3 per cent, to US$98.60 a barrel by 1129 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures edged up by 48 cents, or 0.5 per cent, to US$91.00.
The Brent contract is on track for a 16 per cent decline this week, which would be its steepest weekly percentage fall since the start of the Covid-19 pandemic and its biggest in absolute terms in LSEG data going back to 1988.
WTI is set for a 13 per cent decline.
The oil price slide comes against the backdrop of a dramatic rout in technology stocks.
A potential Iran war de-escalation could lead to more crude exports out of the region.
Signs of an emerging supply excess amid demand destruction were reinforced by spot premiums for Middle Eastern crude benchmarks returning to levels reached before the conflict.
"The crude market is loosening to a state of oversupply based on the balance, but the quality difference still exists as refiners recover what they can take versus what is available," said Rystad oil market analyst Janiv Shah, pointing to longer voyages and the need for ship-to-ship transfers as workarounds near Hormuz.
"The market is still looking for evidence of a firm deal being signed (on Iran), or any backlash from either party could tighten fundamentals once more."
Oil prices fell eight per cent on Wednesday alone after the Democrats swept the US midterm elections, settling at two-month lows.
However, prices rebounded on a surge in tanker attacks in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, renewing concerns over supply flows from the region.
Data from Britain's maritime security agency UKMTO suggested that attacks on oil-carrying ships are still running at close to record pace.
"Oil doesn't have to be at US$117 to be expensive, and a fall to US$93 doesn't mean the underlying problems have disappeared," said Matt Stanley from tanker trackers and energy flow analysts Kpler.
"After over 25 years in this business, I honestly can't recall many weeks quite like this one."

Title: UAE shares fall as geopolitical uncertainty keeps traders cautious
Article:
Stock markets in the United Arab Emirates declined on Friday as geopolitical uncertainty in the region weighed on investor sentiment and kept traders cautious.
Abu Dhabi's benchmark index dropped 1.3 per cent to hit an 18-month low, weighed down by a 1.7 per cent fall in real estate giant Aldar Properties.
The UAE's largest listed conglomerate, International Holding , slumped 2.8 per cent to a more than four-year low after reporting that third-quarter net profit fell more than 28 per cent to 6.22 billion dirhams (US$1.69 billion), from 8.70 billion dirhams a year earlier.
"UAE stock markets will likely remain sensitive to security developments in the region as investors keep a close eye on diplomatic progress and any deal that improves shipping conditions in the Strait of Hormuz," said Mahmoud Mashal, senior market analyst at VT Markets Dubai.
Dubai's main index eased 0.3 per cent, breaking a four-session winning streak, pressured by losses in financial and industrial sector stocks.
Top lender Emirates NBD fell 1.3 per cent, while toll operator Salik Company slipped 1.1 per cent.
However, Emaar Development gained 1.2 per cent after its parent, Emaar Properties, said it intends to make a voluntary cash offer for up to 100 per cent of its shares.
Emaar Properties' shares closed 0.2 per cent lower.
Emaar Properties unveiled its plan on Wednesday to launch an offer to buy the stake it does not already own in its construction arm Emaar Development in a potential deal worth as much as US$3.43 billion.
Emaar Properties, which owns just over 79 per cent of Emaar Development, plans to offer 15 dirhams per share for the outstanding stake under a voluntary cash offer, it said in a filing.
Brent crude was up 0.5 per cent at US$98.73 a barrel by 1155 GMT.
Abu Dhabi's index fell 0.8 per cent for the week, while Dubai's index rose 4.4 per cent, its biggest weekly gain in more than six months, according to LSEG data.

Title: Asyraf: Delaying Najib's house arrest would defy King's decree
Article:

He urged all parties to respect the King's constitutional powers of pardon under Article 42(1) and (2) of the Federal Constitution.

Asyraf said the King, through the Pardons Board, had already made a decision and imposed conditions that had since been fulfilled.
"What is the need to further delay the implementation of house arrest when the fine has been paid in full?" he asked.

Title: British Airways owner sees profits hit by soaring jet fuel costs
Article:
LONDON: The owner of British Airways has revealed a sharp drop in quarterly earnings on surging fuel prices due to the Iran war and warned its annual fuel bill is set to jump to nearly €9 billion (US$10 billion), reported PA Media/dpa.
International Airlines Group (IAG) said pre-tax profits fell 12.9 per cent to €1.63 billion in the three months to Sept 30, while operating profits slumped 15.9 per cent to €1.73 billion.
It said a 4.5 per cent rise in revenues was not enough to offset a 30.4 per cent jump in jet fuel costs, as well as disruption caused by Air Traffic Control outages.
An incident at National Air Traffic Services (NATS) on September 8 led to the cancellation of more than 2,000 flights and impacted hundreds of thousands of passengers.
IAG said its total fuel costs are expected to soar to €8.9 billion for the financial year, even with actions to fix prices in advance.
It said ongoing efforts to drive savings were helping limit the impact of disruption and non-fuel costs.
Luis Gallego, IAG chief executive, said: "As a result of the actions we are taking the outlook for the rest of the year, as well as the start of next year, is positive."

Title: Sterling dips as stock rout boosts dollar, outweighs rate rise boost
Article:
LONDON: The pound fell against the dollar on Friday, as a stock market selloff hit currencies more geared towards global growth, while holding broadly steady against the euro around a 19-month high.
"The market impact of yesterday's Bank of England (BoE) policy update was overshadowed by the deepening selloff for AI-related investments," said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst at MUFG.
The major domestic event of the week was Thursday's BoE meeting, which saw a rate rise and strong hints that at least one further increase will be needed, barring a sudden de-escalation in the Gulf and a fall in oil prices.
Tech stocks tumbled on Wall Street on Thursday, and Asia on Friday, before broadening out in European trading, giving a boost to the dollar.
The pound was last at US$1.3399, down 0.4 per cent, though roughly flat on the week due to gains in earlier sessions.
It was at 83.41 pence per euro, steady on the day and week, and close to its highest since March 2025 which it hit Thursday in the aftermath of the BoE meeting.
"The pound has recently been supported by growing optimism over stronger UK growth, higher UK yields and fiscal concerns becoming a bigger market issue in the euro area than in the UK," said Hardman.
The BoE policy update should reinforce sterling's bullish momentum heading into year-end, but one risk for the currency would be a deeper selloff for AI stocks, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib house arrest: Police remove cordon near his residence

Title: MARC downgraded Zetrix AI's RM2bil IMTN to DIS
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has downgraded Zetrix AI Bhd's RM2 billion Islamic Medium-Term Notes Programme to a default rating of DIS after the company failed to settle an outstanding RM25 million payment due today.
In a statement, the rating agency said the downgrade followed its earlier decision to lower Zetrix AI's rating to CIS on Oct 30.
"Accordingly, MARC Ratings will no longer provide analytical coverage on Zetrix AI," it said.
The development comes amid mounting financial and corporate governance concerns surrounding the company, including its outstanding payment obligations and regulatory scrutiny.
On Oct 30, MARC Ratings downgraded Zetrix AI's sukuk rating to CIS from BB+IS, citing heightened uncertainty over the company's ability to resolve a breach of its sukuk covenant.
The breach involved a requirement for Zetrix AI founder and group managing director Wong Thean Soon to remain the company's single largest shareholder.
The company had yet to remedy the breach or secure a waiver from sukukholders following an unsuccessful meeting on Oct 23.
Separately, Bursa Malaysia today directed Zetrix AI to address the non-payment of its 2025 final dividend by Nov 23, and disclose material information concerning its financial position and governance issues by Nov 11.

Title: Families of 54 Malaysians killed in Nepal-Tibet floods to receive RM10,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Families of the 54 Malaysians who died in the Nepal-Tibet flood tragedy on Aug 26 will receive a one-off payment of RM10,000 each through the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma).
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the decision was made by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim following detailed discussions at today's cabinet meeting.
"We discussed it at length in the cabinet, and the prime minister decided that a one-off payment of RM10,000 will be given to each victim's family, but they must follow the list set out under Nadma.
"This means there is an order of priority. For example, the priority is the wife or husband, the second is the parents, and the third is the children.
"We will issue the list," he told reporters after visiting the 24th Deepavali Carnival 2026 at Bukit Jalil National Stadium here today.
Ramanan said he had directed Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra) director-general K. Raveendran Nair to obtain detailed information from the Finance Ministry and contact the victims' next of kin soon.
The devastating flood and debris flow on Aug 26, triggered by a glacial ice and rock avalanche in the upper catchment area of Lhende Khola in Tibet, has claimed 1,451 lives.
About 5,700 people, including more than 600 foreign nationals, are still reported missing.

Title: Hektar REIT cancels EGM on RM125mil KYS KL East International School acquisition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hektar Real Estate Investment Trust (Hektar REIT) has announced the cancellation of its upcoming unitholders' extraordinary general meeting (EGM), which was originally scheduled for Nov 16.
The cancelled meeting was called to seek unitholders' approval for the proposed acquisition of leasehold interest in part of a land in Setapak, together with the existing buildings and a new one to be constructed there, comprising of an international and private school known as KYS KL East International School from KYS College Sdn Bhd (KCSB).
The transaction carries a purchase consideration of RM125 million, to be satisfied via a cash payment of RM106.55 million alongside the allotment and issuance of new ordinary units in Hektar REIT valued at RM18.45 million.
The cancellation stems from unresolved conditions tied to the deal's sale and purchase agreement (SPA).
Following an assessment, the REIT manager's board noted that certain conditions precedent remain outstanding. Consequently, the board requires further clarification from the vendor, KCSB, regarding the progress and status of their fulfillment.
In deciding to cancel the meeting, the board emphasized that the move was made in the best interests of Hektar REIT and its unitholders.
The pause will allow the manager, Hektar Asset Management Sdn Bhd, to seek the necessary clarifications and evaluate any potential implications on the terms or structure of the proposed acquisition and lease.
According to the official document, this approach ensures that the manager can "assess whether any further action or consideration is required, before seeking unitholders' approval".
The board believes that delaying the vote will ultimately present unitholders with a more complete and updated position on the acquisition, enabling a more informed decision should a fresh EGM be called.
Despite the delay, the board explicitly clarified that the cancellation of the unitholders' meeting does not constitute a termination of the SPA or the proposed acquisition and lease.
Hektar Asset Management will continue to monitor the vendor's progress in fulfilling the outstanding conditions and will make the necessary announcements regarding any material developments, including the decision to convene a fresh unitholders' meeting when deemed appropriate.

Title: Najib returns to Kajang Prison after HKL medical check-up
Article:
KAJANG: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, who underwent a medical examination at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) this evening, returned to Kajang Prison here tonight.
The grey Proton X70 sports utility vehicle (SUV) carrying the former Pekan member of parliament arrived at the prison complex at 7.15pm, accompanied by Malaysian Prisons Department escort vehicles.
Earlier today, the media reported that the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) had called for the implementation of Najib's house arrest to be temporarily deferred pending further clarification on the interpretation of the Conditional Pardon Order granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim.
In a statement, the A-GC said the deferral followed legal questions surrounding the interpretation of the order dated Sept 18, 2026, particularly the implications of the RM50 million fine payment on the remainder of Najib's prison sentence in the SRC International case.
Najib, 73, was earlier reported to have undergone a medical examination at HKL after the vehicle carrying him was seen leaving the Kajang Prison complex this evening.
A source said Najib returned to prison after completing the examination as several matters needed to be settled there before any subsequent movement.
Najib was reported to have settled the RM50 million fine imposed on him in the SRC International Sdn Bhd funds misappropriation case today. This was confirmed by his lawyer, Muhammad Farhan Shafee.
On Sept 18, Najib received a conditional pardon from the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Najib was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million after the Kuala Lumpur High Court found him guilty on July 28, 2020, of seven charges involving the misappropriation of RM42 million belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.
On Aug 23, 2022, the Federal Court dismissed Najib's final appeal and upheld his conviction and sentence. He began serving his prison term at Kajang Prison on the same day.
Najib subsequently submitted a pardon petition to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on Sept 2, 2022. The application was considered at a Pardons Board meeting on Jan 29, 2024.

Title: Bank Negara takes action against two entities over unapproved advertising of foreign currency services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia has taken enforcement action against Najmuldin Exchanger and Nusantara Global Network over suspected contraventions of the Financial Services Act 2013 (FSA).
The action relates to the advertising of foreign currency buying and selling activities without the central bank's written approval.
"The enforcement action was undertaken by Bank Negara with the assistance of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), as part of Bank Negara's continuous enforcement efforts to safeguard the public against potential financial risks associated with the unauthorised buying and selling of foreign currency.
"A total of four premises in various parts of Kedah and Perak were searched. Relevant documents, equipment, books and digital devices were seized to facilitate the investigation," the central bank said in a statement published on its website today.
It noted that the entities are being investigated under subsection 214(2) read together with paragraph 1(b) of Schedule 14 of the FSA.
Bank Negara said members of the public are advised to refrain from participating in unlicensed or unregistered entities offering or advertising foreign currency-related services, as this may result in being complicit in illegal activities.
"For further information on illegal financial schemes and enforcement actions taken by Bank Negara, please refer to bnm.gov.my/enforcement-actions," it emphasised.
Bank Negara added that members of the public with information on any person or entity suspected of advertising or facilitating the buying or selling of foreign currency without authorisation may report the matter to Bank Negara at bnm.gov.my/BNMLINK or 1300-88-5465.
